name: HAIEC Why Use HAIEC: Buyer-Intent/Use-Case Library
status: RESEARCH-BASED HYPOTHESES, NOT MEASURED KEYWORD DEMAND OR CLAIMS OF CURRENT CUSTOMER OUTCOMES
terms: Buyer questions and exact search phrases are editorial hypotheses. P0/P1/P2 are conversion/editorial prioritization, not Semrush search volumes or proven SERP rankings.

entries.question: Our AI pilot works, but security will not approve production
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent POC stuck security approval
entries.value: Unblock a stalled AI pilot with a scoped, evidence-backed production-readiness review.

entries.question: Can we safely deploy this AI agent?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent production readiness assessment
entries.value: Make a defensible release decision from actual action paths, authority and applicable evidence.

entries.question: We need evidence before releasing an agent
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent deployment approval evidence
entries.value: Document what was assessed, what remains unresolved and who owns the next decision.
entries.truthBoundary: Separate U5 verdict from human deployment approval

entries.question: How do we take an AI agent from proof of concept to production?
entries.searchPhrase: AI POC to production governance checklist
entries.value: Move beyond model demos to a review of consequential actions, controls and missing proof.

entries.question: Do our controls still apply after the latest agent release?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent release change security assessment
entries.value: Compare source versions and evidence boundaries before relying on an earlier evaluation.

entries.question: Will our AI pass architecture and risk review?
entries.searchPhrase: enterprise AI architecture risk review
entries.value: Give architecture, security and business owners a shared source-backed decision basis.
entries.truthBoundary: Evidence is limited to scoped system

entries.question: What can our AI agent actually change?
entries.searchPhrase: what actions can AI agent take tools API
entries.value: Map supported paths from an agent through tools and APIs to business operations and resources.
entries.truthBoundary: Code reachable does not prove execution

entries.question: Is this AI agent overprivileged?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent excessive permissions audit
entries.value: Compare tool capabilities, relevant authority and actual grants where source evidence is available.

entries.question: Who authorized the AI to make that decision?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent delegated authority governance
entries.value: Determine whether the business choice was fixed by policy or legitimately delegated to the agent.

entries.question: Does our AI have access it should not have?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent IAM permission risk assessment
entries.value: Expose relevant mismatches between approved boundaries, effective grants and source capability.
entries.truthBoundary: Do not infer effective grants from code

entries.question: How do we enforce human review for consequential AI actions?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent human approval controls
entries.value: Review action-bound approval evidence and the actual mediation boundary for material decisions.

entries.question: Can a child agent exceed its parent's authority?
entries.searchPhrase: multi agent delegation security assessment
entries.value: Trace parent-child authority continuity and clarify unresolved actor and scope joins.
entries.truthBoundary: Full identity chain may require connected sources

entries.question: Which systems can my AI agents reach?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent attack surface action path map
entries.value: See supported agent, tool, credential and resource relationships and the consequences they enable.
entries.truthBoundary: Supported reach only, unknown paths remain unknown

entries.question: How do we secure MCP servers and AI tools?
entries.searchPhrase: MCP server security tool permission assessment
entries.value: Inspect tool exposure, server-side checks, privilege boundaries and source-linked action paths.
entries.truthBoundary: Safe scoped test and access rights required

entries.question: Could prompt injection make our agent take harmful actions?
entries.searchPhrase: prompt injection agent tool consequences
entries.value: Follow unsafe input-to-tool paths and identify where actual server authorization is required.
entries.truthBoundary: Risk path is not necessarily exploited

entries.question: Can one tenant's AI see another tenant's data?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent tenant isolation audit
entries.value: Examine trusted tenant-to-principal binding and protected resource access, not just a tenant parameter.

entries.question: Can our RAG agent leak confidential information?
entries.searchPhrase: RAG data leakage security assessment
entries.value: Map protected retrieval, response audience and egress paths with precise source limitations.

entries.question: Are privileged agent API calls properly controlled?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent privileged API authorization assessment
entries.value: Review which privileged actions are technically reachable and whether server-side restrictions apply.
entries.truthBoundary: Guard configuration is not verified enforcement

entries.question: Is an AI scanner finding an actual security risk?
entries.searchPhrase: AI security scanner false positive evidence
entries.value: Separate raw rule matches, source-qualified security findings, path reachability and target effects.
entries.truthBoundary: Scan coverage and source semantics matter

entries.question: What did our agent actually do?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent action audit trail evidence
entries.value: Separate available code paths and permissions from qualified action-correlated observations.

entries.question: Are our AI agents continuously monitored?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent continuous monitoring audit
entries.value: Check each connected runtime source's freshness, scope and coverage before making a monitoring claim.

entries.question: Did the AI guardrail really block that action?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent guardrail enforcement verification
entries.value: Distinguish policy decision, dispatch, provider acknowledgment and independently witnessed target outcome.
entries.truthBoundary: Customer-native PEP integration may be missing

entries.question: Can we shut down a runaway agent?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent kill switch containment effectiveness
entries.value: Assess which stopping or containment controls are actually wired and what target-side evidence is available.
entries.truthBoundary: Do not promise universal kill switch

entries.question: How do we investigate a suspicious agent action?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent incident response investigation evidence
entries.value: Correlate qualified alerts, actor identity, source findings and missing target witnesses.

entries.question: When is it safe to restart the agent after an incident?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent recovery authorization retesting
entries.value: Document scoped retest, accountable human decision and pending effect reconciliation.

entries.question: How do we prepare evidence for an AI regulator or auditor?
entries.searchPhrase: AI audit evidence readiness agentic systems
entries.value: Create an inspectable report basis with source references, limitations and verification records where issued.

entries.question: Can we trust this AI assurance report?
entries.searchPhrase: verify AI assurance report evidence receipt
entries.value: Read what the report established, what was not assessed and what a decision receipt actually verifies.

entries.question: We need reproducible AI audit findings
entries.searchPhrase: deterministic AI assurance evidence report
entries.value: Use frozen evaluation and source-bound report outputs to support repeatable evidence review.

entries.question: How can we prove controls are operating?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent control operating effectiveness evidence
entries.value: Separate cataloged controls, observed findings, executed tests, human review and target-native effect proof.

entries.question: How do we demonstrate AI governance to our board?
entries.searchPhrase: board AI agent risk oversight evidence
entries.value: Translate consequential paths and source limitations into an accountable executive decision packet.

entries.question: What evidence is missing from this AI review?
entries.searchPhrase: AI assurance evidence gap assessment
entries.value: Identify the smallest additional authoritative source needed to answer an unresolved control or action claim.

entries.question: Can we trust this AI vendor before buying?
entries.searchPhrase: third party AI agent vendor due diligence
entries.value: Ask for source, authority, tool and deployment proof beyond a vendor questionnaire, within accessible evidence.

entries.question: Is this vendor's AI safe to connect to our systems?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent vendor security assessment integrations
entries.value: Assess what a supplier agent could access or change through enterprise APIs and tools.
entries.truthBoundary: Requires access to actual integration configuration

entries.question: Can our customers audit our AI SaaS feature?
entries.searchPhrase: AI SaaS customer assurance evidence package
entries.value: Share appropriately bounded technical findings and supported verification artifacts with customer reviewers.

entries.question: Does a vendor's SOC 2 prove their AI agents are safe?
entries.searchPhrase: SOC 2 AI agent security gap third party
entries.value: Separate organizational controls attestations from an agent's reachable actions and authorization evidence.
entries.truthBoundary: SOC 2 is not source path proof

entries.question: How do we review our suppliers' embedded AI?
entries.searchPhrase: AI supplier subprocessors action audit
entries.value: Map consequential third-party AI actions and evidence gaps, with a scoped due diligence record.
entries.truthBoundary: Black-box vendors cannot claim full source coverage

entries.question: Can we assess AI agents from our IDE or CI/CD?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent assurance developer IDE MCP
entries.value: Use authorized source and HAIEC MCP-assisted workflow to request deterministic evaluation and inspect outputs.

entries.question: How do we verify an agent tool change before release?
entries.searchPhrase: AI agent tool schema release audit
entries.value: Compare relevant tool and source paths with their frozen evaluated versions and close new evidence gaps.

entries.question: We already use scanners, IAM and GRC. What is missing?
entries.searchPhrase: AI assurance complement SAST IAM GRC
entries.value: Connect qualified outputs to consequential action and authority questions instead of replacing existing tools.

entries.question: Our scanner tests pass. Is the AI agent ready?
entries.searchPhrase: AI security testing vs production assurance
entries.value: Relate component tests to protected action, delegated choice, identity, policy and observed effect gaps.

entries.question: Can we approve AI agents that move money?
entries.searchPhrase: AI payment agent authorization audit
entries.value: Review recipient/amount choice, applicable authority, effective access and observed payment effect separately.

entries.question: Can we deploy AI touching sensitive healthcare data?
entries.searchPhrase: healthcare AI agent audit evidence access control
entries.value: Assess access paths and evidence for protected data actions before relying on operational safety claims.

entries.question: How do we assess AI agents writing to ERP or MES?
entries.searchPhrase: manufacturing AI agent ERP MES assurance
entries.value: Follow procurement, supplier and manufacturing system write paths with qualified source and authority checks.
entries.truthBoundary: Demo vs actual plant effects distinct

entries.question: How do we control AI-initiated network changes?
entries.searchPhrase: telecom network AI agent change assurance
entries.value: Investigate OSS/BSS and network control paths, qualified permissions and resulting evidence.

entries.question: Can we audit AI claims or underwriting decisions?
entries.searchPhrase: insurance AI agent claims decision audit
entries.value: Examine consequential decisions, delegated authority, source/identity scope and audit artifacts.
entries.truthBoundary: No fair outcome or compliance guarantee

entries.question: Is our HR screening AI evidence ready for oversight?
entries.searchPhrase: hiring AI oversight evidence audit
entries.value: Qualify applicable assessment and evidence coverage for specific hiring decisions and access paths.
entries.truthBoundary: Do not claim full bias audit from action paths alone
